chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abu Jameela Al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Jabir ibn Yazeed, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And speak to the people good words', he said: 'Speak to the people the best of what you love to be said about yourselves'.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'speak good to people' mean according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the Quranic command 'speak good to people' by defining 'good' as uttering the finest qualities or words one desires for oneself, thereby establishing a principle of ethical reciprocity. This interpretation, recorded in al-Kafi, highlights the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and the psychological dimension of social conduct, linking verbal kindness directly to self-respect and mutual dignity within the community.
